measurement: MP-AX1 IME pointer-path execution test and native Command Palette focus restoration observation
candidate: the commit that introduces palette.rs and this evidence directory at the recorded source hash

execution_path_test.change: palette_invoke_slot (the pointer route) now delegates to pointer_activation(...), which applies the composition guard and re-derives availability for one inventory slot. The test module calls that exact function, not only the palette_dispatch_allowed predicate.

assertion_sensitivity.mutation: the pointer_activation composition guard was replaced with `if !open` (guard removed)
assertion_sensitivity.result: FAILED: assertion `left == right` failed; left: Some((ShowArtifact, None)); right: None; test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed

native_observation.command: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File probe.ps1 (driver stored beside this file; it waits on the shared C:/tmp/cos-desktop-native.lock directory and removes it afterwards)
native_observation.driver: synthetic window messages: WM_MOUSEMOVE/WM_LBUTTONDOWN/WM_LBUTTONUP for the click, keybd_event(VK_CONTROL) + WM_KEYDOWN/WM_KEYUP for Ctrl+K, WM_CHAR for text, WM_KEYDOWN/WM_KEYUP for Escape and Enter
native_observation.why_synthetic: the window cannot be granted foreground focus in this session (SetForegroundWindow fails; recorded in docs/development/evidence-published/REPRODUCING.md), so a real keyboard session is unavailable. The messages enter the application's own window procedure and input handler; no product behaviour was changed for the observation.

environment.profile_isolation: fresh LOCALAPPDATA per run under C:/dev/cos-desktop/target/ax1-native-<guid>, deleted after the run. Deviation from the C:/tmp guideline is measured: an isolated LOCALAPPDATA under C:/tmp and under %TEMP% makes the instance guard refuse startup with open-lock-file on this sandboxed host, while the workspace target path starts normally.

reads: TASK_SEARCH after_click_x='x' (the click focused the invoking rail search; the typed character landed there)

PALETTE_OPEN delta=9; palette dialog exposed as ControlType.Window named 'コマンドパレット'; query field ControlType.Edit named 'コマンド検索' with ValuePattern value 'コマンドを入力…'; 11 ListItems present (available rows expose InvokePattern; unavailable rows do not)
PALETTE_INPUT after_abc='abc' (text entry landed in the palette while the invoking control kept 'x')
AFTER_ESCAPE palette_delta=-5 palette_keys_left=0 rail_present=True (every element introduced by the palette is gone)
AFTER_ESCAPE rail_value='xz' (after Escape, typing 'z' changed the invoking rail search value from 'x' to 'xz' and reached no other control)
REOPEN palette_delta=14; AFTER_ENTER palette_delta=0 descendant_count=51 (Enter on the active row closed the palette through the keyboard activation path)
uia_limits: GPUI exposes no UIA focus property (no HasKeyboardFocus/FocusedElement provider exists in the pinned gpui_windows source), so focus restoration is observed behaviourally: after Escape, a typed character changes the invoking rail search value and reaches no other control.
Palette elements carry no AutomationId; they were identified by UIA Name/ControlType and by diffing the element set across the open/close boundary.

task-search is ControlType.Edit and supports ValuePattern but not InvokePattern; the accessibility Click listener was therefore exercised with a synthetic mouse click at its UIA bounding rectangle (DPI 96, 1:1).
No screen-reader announcement, preedit rendering, caret/selection during composition, TSF internals, real keyboard repeat or AT quality is claimed.
native_observation.result: The palette opened through the Ctrl+K keyboard path, accepted query text, closed on Escape with the invoking control focused again (behavioural proof), and closed on Enter through the keyboard activation path.

limits: One run on one machine (Windows 11 10.0.26300, 96 DPI).
Synthetic window messages, not a real keyboard or mouse session; the window could not be foregrounded.
No UIA focus property exists for GPUI elements; focus restoration is behavioural, not an accessibility-tree property.
The composition-guard test is in-process (unit execution path), not a native IME session; no IME preedit/candidate-window claim is made.
Fixture mode (task-184) only; no Runtime connection or real authorization is involved.
No AT quality, screen-reader acceptance, High Contrast or DPI claim.
